About

Khrystian E. King, LL.D, M.S.W., L.C.S.W. was born in Massachusetts to Leon and Gloree King, who emigrated from the island of Bermuda. Khrystian has been a Licensed Social Worker for the Massachusetts Department of Children and Families for the last 25 years. He has worked tirelessly to protect, support and empower children and their families throughout the Worcester Area. Khrystian is the former Regional Vice President of SEIU Local 509's DCF Chapter and a former member of the National Association of Social Workers. He was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Laws conferred by Wheaton College in 2020 for his advocacy for the empowerment of Worcester's children, youth and families.

As a man of many "Firsts," in 2016 Councilor King became the first African American male to serve since 1936, the first African American man to ever be elected city-wide; Khrystian is the longest serving At-Large elected official of color in Worcester's municipal history. In 2024 he became the first Black Vice Chair of the Worcester City Council. He is a co-founder of Black Families Together, a Worcester organization that addresses systemic racism. He is also a co-founder of the Black and Latinx Municipal Caucus, a statewide group of BIPOC elected officials. Councilor King is serving his sixth two-year term as Councilor-at-Large.

Education

Khrystian attended Holy Name and St. Peter-Marian High Schools. He graduated from Wheaton College with a Bachelor of Arts in Social Psychology, and later earned his Master of Social Work from Simmons College and a Master of Public Administration (MPA)-Certified in Public Management and Leadership from the Moakley Center for Public Management at Suffolk University.

Governance

As Vice Chairman Khrystian King remains focused on strengthening Worcester through leadership grounded in accountability, equity, and responsiveness to residents. His priorities include expanding truly affordable housing options, supporting working families, improving schools, and advancing public health and safety. With decades of experience as a child protective Social Worker, he emphasizes policies that uplift vulnerable populations, address homelessness, and ensure that every neighborhood benefits from city services. King continues to advocate for transparent, community-centered governance that brings residents into the decision-making process, strengthens youth and family supports, and ensures people receive a fair return on their tax dollars through well-maintained streets, sidewalks, and essential services. His work reflects a commitment to building a Worcester where longtime residents, new arrivals, and future generations can thrive.

Personal Facts

Khrystian is married to Tatiana King M.S.W. / L.I.C.S.W. and has three beautiful daughters: Jailyn, Alexandra and Leiyani. His eldest daughter Jailyn is also a M.S.W. / L.C.S.W. clinician. The King family is a family of Social Workers in the City of Worcester.

About

Dr. Satya Mitra is serving his first two-year term as a City Councilor-At-Large. Dr. Mitra is the first person elected to the Worcester City Council of Indian descent. Born in India, Dr. Mitra migrated to the US in 1976 with a Ph.D. in Biochemistry to pursue biomedical research and has lived in Worcester for the last 40 years. Almost fifteen years later, Dr. Mitra founded The Guru Tax & Financial Services Inc. that assisted countless families and businesses in Worcester and across the country. Prior to being elected to the Worcester City Council, Dr. Mitra has served the Worcester Planning Board, Worcester Library Board, Worcester State University Foundation, Quinsigamond Community College Board, Worcester Regional Chamber of Commerce, and the Greater Worcester Community Foundation. His work has been and continues to be guided by a belief in the importance of education, economic empowerment, and community engagement.

Education

Dr. Mitra received his B.Sc. in Biology and Chemistry from Jabalpur University, India in 1970. In 1973 he received his M.Sc. in Biochemistry from Nagpur University, India and then continued his education by earning his Ph.D. in Biochemistry from Nagpur University. In 1989 he became an Enrolled Agent with the license to practice tax laws by the IRS and he became a Certified Financial Planner at the Denver College of Financial Planning in 1993.

Personal Facts

Dr. Mitra has received numerous awards, including the Key to the City of Worcester, Worcester Business Journal Hall of Fame Inductee, named one of the most 100 influential professionals in Central Massachusetts, and the Harvey-Ball Smile Award Recipient for his humanitarian efforts. In 2019, Dr. Mitra published his book The 5 C's that quickly climbed the ranks and made Amazon's best sellers list. Satya and his wife, Sheema, have their own tax consulting business that has been helping the Worcester community for over 30 years. The married couple then established Joy Guru Humanitarian Services - a charitable foundation aimed at offering hope and help to underprivileged people. Dr. Mitra has two sons, Abiskar who is a sports lawyer, and Alingon who is a professional stand-up comedian.

About

Kathleen M. "Kate" Toomey is a Post-Release/Reintegration Specialist with the Worcester County Sheriff's Office, bringing more than a decade of experience in the healthcare and addiction field and over thirty years of service in community and external affairs. She is an active member of several working groups addressing issues related to addiction and homelessness.

Councilor Toomey has chaired numerous City Council committees, including Education, Traffic and Parking, Public Works, and Public Safety. Her professional background includes teaching in the Boston Public Schools and the Central Massachusetts Collaborative, work as an Art Therapist, and experience as a small business owner.

She is currently serving her eleventh two-year term as a Councilor-at-Large. Previously, Councilor Toomey served three two-year terms on the Worcester School Committee and was Vice Chair during her final term.

Education

Councilor Toomey is a graduate of Mount St. Joseph Academy in Boston. She earned a Bachelor of Arts in Art and Education from Regis College, Weston, and completed graduate coursework in Public Administration at Northeastern University in Boston.

Objectives

Councilor Toomey believes that community policing and public safety are among the City's highest priorities. She also supports responsible business growth and initiatives that improve quality of life, including maintaining safe streets, sidewalks, and infrastructure.

Personal Facts

Councilor Toomey is married to Stephen R. Toomey and is the mother of three children and the grandmother of three.

About

Robert Bilotta is serving his first two-year term as District Two Councilor. He is a disability rights and housing advocate and currently serves on the Board of Directors for the Center for Living & Working. Prior to being elected, Councilor Bilotta served on the Worcester Human Rights Commission and chair of the Worcester Together Affordable Housing Coalition.

As a lifelong District Two resident, he understands issues facing the neighborhoods and is committed to improving quality of life by bringing residents, families, businesses, and community stakeholders together.

Councilor Bilotta believes in transparent and accessible local government that works for residents of all abilities and backgrounds. He also believes Worcester's economic development should foster affordable housing and thriving neighborhoods.

District Two generally includes the following neighborhoods: Lincoln Square, Lincoln Street, Brittan Square, lower Burncoat, UMass, Lake Avenue north of Hamilton Street, Bloomingdale, Shrewsbury and Franklin Streets, Poet's Hill, Plumley Village, downtown east of Main Street, WPI, Chadwick Square, Indian Lake, the Canal District north of Kelley Square and Grafton Hill north of Hamilton Street.

Education

Councilor Bilotta is a graduate of North High School and received a bachelor's degree in Communications and Urban Studies from Worcester State University.

Personal Facts

Councilor Bilotta is a proud uncle, local history enthusiast, and enjoys spending time with friends and family.

About

Luis A. Ojeda is serving his second two-year term as Worcester's District Four Councilor. Luis was born and raised in Worcester and is of Dominican and Puerto Rican heritage. As a lifelong resident and dedicated member of the local community, he understands issues facing the City and makes it his purpose to give back. Luis actively demonstrates his commitment to Worcester by engaging individuals, families, businesses and community leaders in advocating for initiatives that help to improve the quality of community life.

Residing in Worcester, Luis has served as an Educator in the Worcester Public Schools for over 20 years. He is currently an Assistant Principal, youth sports coach and mentor, and directs programs focused on student growth and development and creating access to advancement opportunities.

District Four generally includes the following neighborhoods: Green Island, Kelley Square, lower Vernon Hill, the Canal District south of Kelley Square, Four Corners, Main South, South Worcester, Piedmont, Crown Hill, downtown west of Main Street, Gardner/Boys & Girls Club Way/Hammond, Clark University, Webster Square, and Highland Street east of Park Avenue.

Education

Luis holds a Master of Education in Organizational Management from Endicott College and a Bachelor of Science degree in Sports Management from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst. He is a graduate of Worcester's Doherty Memorial High School and Quinsigamond Community College.

Objectives

Luis is passionate about issues concerning working individuals, families and local organizations. He believes in creating opportunities for all community stakeholders to collaborate and take a proactive approach in helping to ensure local government can be responsive to prevalent needs and concerns that will further community building efforts. He is focused on innovation and the development of progressive policies encompassing equitable education, public health and safety, affordable housing and racial, social and economic justice. Amongst other efforts, he works on transformative development initiatives to improve District 4 neighborhoods.

Personal Facts

Luis is a devoted husband and father to his three children. He is the co-founder of TLK Sports and Worcester Team United. He was recognized as an Exceptional Latino Educator by Latinos for Education and the Massachusetts House of Representatives for outstanding contributions in the local community. He received the Worcester Red Sox Diamond Sports Award, and in addition to other community achievement awards, Luis is also a recipient of the Worcester Public Schools Thomas Jefferson Award for public service.

Morris A. Bergman, a Worcester attorney in private practice, is serving his seventh consecutive two-year term as a Councilor-at-Large. He previously served two terms as a member of the City of Worcester Zoning Board of Appeals and currently serves as a board member and docent for Preservation Worcester.

Education

He is a graduate of Doherty Memorial High School in Worcester. He received a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration and a Juris Doctorate, both from Boston University.

Personal Facts

He is married to Wendy (Bonnett) Bergman, MD and is the father of three children, Max (married to Baila), Micah, and Hanna. He is also a new grandfather to his granddaughter, Paisley, and has a dog named Lucy. He enjoys American history and advocating for recognition of Worcester's role in it, along with gardening and antique collecting.

About

Gary Rosen, a retired high school teacher whose career included seventeen years at Doherty Memorial High School, is the only Worcester elected official ever who has served as a School Committee member and as both an At-Large and District City Councilor. His lifetime of service to the youth, adults, and seniors of our city includes having served as the chairman of the Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) Advisory Board, a member of the Board of Health, and the summer voice of the Massachusetts Symphony Orchestra at Institute Park. He has been a volunteer leader with the Friends of the Worcester Senior Center for over 20 years and has extensive local radio and TV experience. Finally, he chooses to have no social media presence, preferring to interact with his constituents in person, by email, or phone.

Education

Councilor At-Large Rosen is a graduate of Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI) with a Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry and of Worcester State University with a Master of Education degree in counseling.

About

Tony Economou, a lifelong D-1 Worcester resident, has worked as a real estate broker for over 26 years and is serving his fourth term as the District 1 Worcester City Councilor after previously serving three terms from 2011 through 2017. Prior to first being elected to local office, Tony had been involved in Worcester by serving on the Worcester Public Library Board of Trustees, the Worcester Educational Development Foundation, the Civic Center Commission for the DCU Center, and has been a member of the North Worcester Business Association since 1988.

District One generally includes the following neighborhoods: Salisbury Street, Westwood Hills, Assumption College, Hancock Hill, Grove Street, Holden Street, Indian Hill, Indian Lake, Greendale, the Summit, Quinsigamond Community College, upper Burncoat, Clark Street, Lincoln Village, Great Brook Valley, Curtis Apartments, Montvale and Massachusetts Avenue Local Historic Districts, Hammond Heights, Bancroft Tower, Winter Heights and Richmond/Flagg.

Education

Tony is a proud graduate of Worcester Public Schools, graduating from Burncoat High while his 2 boys graduated from Doherty.

Personal Facts

In his spare time, Tony enjoys skiing, heading to the beach, Worcester and Boston sports, enjoying time with family and friends, and helping on various other worthy committees and events in the City.

About

John P. Fresolo is a lifelong resident of District 3 and is currently serving his first two-year term as the District Three Worcester City Councilor. Prior to serving on the City Council, John served as State Representative for the 16th Worcester District in the Massachusetts House of Representatives from January 1999 - May 2013. While serving as State Representative, Mr. Fresolo was instrumental in securing funding for the Route 146 Mass Pike project, bringing Walmart and the Mall at Blackstone, and securing $100,000 earmark for additional community policing in the Grafton Hill, Vernon Hill, and Union Hill neighborhoods for 14 consecutive years. Councilor Fresolo's achievements made him known by his constituents as someone that "gets things done."

District Three generally includes the following neighborhoods: Grafton Hill south of Hamilton Street, Rice Square, Billings Square, Union Hill, upper Vernon Hill, Massasoit, Edgemere, Granite Street, Lake Avenue, Quinsigamond Village and College Hill.

Objectives

John is focused on improving traffic issues in Grafton Hill and Lake Avenue due to CSX locating in Worcester. John will address and solve the Roosevelt School dismissal issues that have plagued that area of Grafton Street for several years. With the high cost of living and lack of senior housing, Councilor Fresolo will advocate for the renovation of the former St. Vincent School of Nursing to be converted into affordable Senior Housing. Staying true to his resume, Councilor Fresolo will concentrate on addressing the city services and needs of Worcester and responding to constituents' requests.

Personal Facts

John is the father of two daughters, Francesca and Maria. He has 2 grandchildren, Sebastian and Alessia. Councilor Fresolo is proud that 3 generations of Fresolos reside in District 3.

About

Councilor Jose A. Rivera is currently serving his first two-year term as District 5 Worcester City Councilor. Born in Philadelphia, Jose was one of 5 children raised by a single mother, whom he lost when he was just 10 years old. Jose moved around with different family members in the US and Puerto Rico before ultimately settling in Worcester at 16 years old, where he graduated South High School and began the pursuit of his dream of becoming a boxing champion. After years of dedication and perseverance, Jose became a three-time world champion in two different weight divisions, capturing his first title, International Boxing Organization Welterweight, in 1997. The same grit and passion that led Jose to international success has brought him to become District 5 City Councilor, pledging to support his constituents and address the issues of Worcester.

District Five generally includes the following neighborhoods: Columbus Park, Stafford Street, Heard Street, Main Street from Webster Square to Cherry Valley, Airport Hill, Botany Bay, Mill Street, June Street, Neighborly Newton, Newton Square, Worcester State College, Tatnuck, West Tatnuck, Beaver Brook and Moreland Hill.

Objectives

Jose has many priorities to promote the residents of District 5 and the entirety of Worcester. Jose is an avid supporter of public safety, improving trust between Law Enforcement and the community, and keeping all levels of government accountable. Jose understands that housing has been a major issue in Worcester and seeks to expand affordable housing options, working with local, state, and federal partners to guarantee that every resident may have a place to call home. Jose also prioritizes expanding youth activities, helping businesses open and stay open in the City, creating sustainable job opportunities, and keeping taxes affordable for the residents and businesses of Worcester.

Personal Facts

Jose is a proud married father of four children, with a stepson, and a 5-year-old grandson.
